C-LARGE-DOC-WAVE-A.Name: Large-document Wave A: progressive mount with frozen-block regions
C-LARGE-DOC-WAVE-A.Summary: Stage 0 isolated Mark's opening cost: on the 1 MB corpus shape, mounting the parsed block tree into the editable DOM costs ~809 ms of an ~890 ms open path while the parse itself is ~20 ms (recorded parse_proxy), and the owner-approved LargeDocumentContract fixes the Wave A targets (ordinary ~100 KB: first visible content within 400 ms, typing p95 within 50 ms; 1 MB: open within 1500 ms, typing p95 within 100 ms; 1.7 MB/9000-section stress: open within 4000 ms, typing p95 within 250 ms, longest main-thread task within 300 ms, scroll p95 within 50 ms) and defers exactly two budget decisions to Wave A: tail-mount completion and time-to-input. Wave A replaces the single synchronous full-document mount behind Muya's setMarkdown entry (src/muya/lib/index.js) with a progressive mount: the document still parses whole (parse is measured-cheap and stays untouched), the visible region plus a margin mounts synchronously to produce first visible content and a usable editor, and the remaining tail mounts incrementally in bounded idle-time slices that never hold the main thread past the contract's longest-task budget, organized as frozen regions — blocks above the furthest mount boundary are never re-mounted — with safe split points chosen at top-level block boundaries (oversized single blocks chunk their content through the same slicing), on-demand region mounting when navigation jumps into the not-yet-mounted tail, a mount-depth/traversal guard for pathological structures, and fail-safe degradation: any chunking failure, guard trip or mount error abandons the progressive attempt and falls back to the legacy single-pass mount so the document always opens. The progressive path ships local, default-off and session-latched behind a new visible Experimental section in preferences per the approved experimental access model; the default path is exactly today's behavior and its existing gates must not move. Wave A extends the Stage 0 harness (M-060) with a tail-mount phase and a budgeted time-to-input metric, proves both paths on the committed corpus in all three evidence tiers, keeps every Stage 0 characterization oracle green under the progressive path, and ends in an owner decision gate that fixes the two deferred budgets (proposed defaults grounded in the recorded baseline: time-to-input within first-visible-content + 250 ms on every shape; tail-mount completion within 1.5x the same-run legacy mount duration per shape with absolute ceilings of 2500 ms at 1 MB and 6000 ms at the stress shape), recorded durably into the LargeDocumentContract before any Wave B work starts. The architectural blueprint (frozen regions, safe split points, surrogate-pair-aware cutting, prefix-mismatch reset, degradation belts) is adapted from an external research digest of the Claude Code 2.1.312 markdown stack carried in design-context.xml — a design reference only, with no code copied and no number inherited without its own Stage 0 grounding.

Problem.Description: Four gaps block large-document usability today. (1) The open path is one synchronous O(document) mount: setMarkdown parses, builds and mounts the entire block tree and WebKit style/layout walks ~30k DOM nodes on the stress shape before anything is visible or editable — the same trajectory that pushed the CI open-timing marker over its budget on a 600 KB document and that Stage 0 measured at ~809 ms of mount per ~890 ms open at 1 MB. (2) The LargeDocumentContract deliberately deferred its last two budgets — tail-mount completion and time-to-input — to Wave A, so Wave A has no success criteria until they are proposed and approved. (3) Muya has no partial mount architecture: every open is a full mount; per-block update machinery exists for edits but nothing mounts a region and defers a tail. (4) The approved experimental access model (local, default-off, session-latched, visible Experimental setting) has no surface to live in — preferences have no Experimental section. An external blueprint exists (Claude Code 2.1.312 research digest, 2026-10-30): its frozen-chunk streaming with stable-prefix boundaries, safe split points that never cut surrogate pairs or open fences, prefix-mismatch reset and four parser-resilience belts is directly adaptable, but it is a terminal streaming renderer over character offsets — Mark's block-tree mount needs its own region model, which is exactly what this change specifies.

Goals.R-1: Progressive mount core behind the Muya mount entry: setMarkdown gains a progressive mode — parse whole (the full document model exists from parse onward, so every model-reading consumer — save, serialization, word count, TOC, search — operates on the complete document at all times; only DOM mounting is progressive), mount the visible region plus a viewport margin synchronously to first visible content and an input-ready editor, then mount the remaining tail incrementally in bounded cooperative slices that yield to input between slices — requestIdleCallback where the engine provides it, a yielding timer/message-channel scheduler on WebKit/WKWebView where requestIdleCallback is unavailable — with a timeout lane that also guarantees tail completion under continuous input, so an always-busy editor never starves the tail; mounted regions are frozen (never re-mounted while the document stays above the furthest mount boundary) and each slice yields as soon as its work budget is exhausted, so no slice holds the main thread past the contract's longest-task budget on the stress shape. A block whose content alone exceeds the synchronous-region budget (the giant-paragraph and giant-code-block corpus shapes) chunks its content through the same bounded-slice mechanism, so single-block documents keep making visible progress instead of regressing to one monolithic mount.
Goals.R-2: Safe split points at block boundaries only: a mount boundary is always a top-level block boundary of the parsed block tree (no character-offset heuristics); text is never sliced inside a surrogate pair (validated offsets only); a tail beginning inside an unresolved construct (for example an open fence) extends the synchronous region to the next safe boundary; if content above a boundary changes underneath the progressive mount (external reload, undo of the open edit, workspace replacement), the affected region is revalidated and remounted, with a full progressive-state reset — falling back to one legacy full mount for that document — as the bounded worst case. Navigation into a not-yet-mounted region (scroll jump, search hit, TOC or link jump, the remembered cursor position restored on open, jump-to-end) mounts the target region on demand before revealing it — the destination is never empty or blank — and continuous scrolling toward the furthest mounted boundary mounts ahead of the reading position (a prefetch margin sized at plan time), so a normally scrolling reader never crosses into unmounted content; this prefetch work is scroll-time work and is governed by the contract's scroll frame budget like any other; the viewport's reading position never shifts as a result of tail mounting alone (scroll anchoring while the document grows), and while the tail mounts the document never appears to end early: reserved layout space or an equivalent non-content indication (mechanism fixed at plan time) marks the still-mounting region.
Goals.R-3: Mount guards and fail-safe degradation: a depth/traversal guard bounds mount recursion (deeply nested or pathological-structure fixtures from the Stage 0 corpus mount with bounded traversal, degrading oversize subtrees to a flat mount rather than unbounded recursion), and a catch-all wraps the progressive path — any chunking failure, guard trip or unexpected error abandons the progressive attempt, clears its partial state and completes the open through the legacy single-pass mount; a fallback that fires after input has been accepted preserves every accepted edit, because the document model is the source of truth and the legacy remount mounts the current model — including edits typed since open — never a stale pre-open snapshot; a content-free marker records which path served each open. There is no reachable state in which a document fails to open or an editor stays blank behind a silent fallback.
Goals.R-4: Experimental access surface per the approved model: a new visible Experimental section in preferences hosts the progressive-mount toggle — local, default-off, session-latched (a relaunch returns it to off; it never persists silently), taking effect for documents opened after the flip without remounting already-open tabs; the UI labels the feature experimental and names the large-document contract it serves, and shows a content-free per-session counter of opens served by the progressive path versus fallback so an enabled user can see when the experiment did not serve an open (no toast, no modal). Whether the enabled path applies to all documents or only above a size threshold is fixed at plan time and recorded either way.
Goals.R-5: Deferred-budget owner gate: a decision document proposes the two contract-deferred budgets with same-run evidence on the committed corpus — time-to-input and tail-mount completion — with defaults of time-to-input within first-visible-content + 250 ms on every shape and tail-mount completion within 1.5x the same-run legacy mount duration per shape with absolute ceilings of 2500 ms at 1 MB and 6000 ms at the stress shape; the same document presents the budget-semantics mapping for explicit ratification — on the progressive path the contract's open budget is satisfied by time-to-input, with first visible content and tail-mount completion reported as separate phases — because the contract's "open" was grounded in Stage 0's full-open measurement and remapping it is an owner call, not an engineering footnote; the owner's approved values land in the LargeDocumentContract (.grace/context/ux-guidelines.xml) through the governance step before any Wave B work starts, and unapproved placeholders are never used as gates.
Goals.R-6: Harness extension on M-060: the bench driver gains a tail-mount phase (open start to full-mount completion) and promotes time-to-input to a budgeted metric — today it is a BLOCK_OPEN field in the real-app acceptance protocol, and the bench tiers gain it through the existing real-input typing injector driven at the earliest input-ready moment, with the exact harness seam fixed at plan time and the acceptance tier remaining the authoritative full-fidelity source (the owner decision notes full TTI wants a tab-lifecycle harness) — emitted for both the legacy and progressive paths on the committed corpus across the existing three evidence tiers. On the progressive path the contract's open budget maps to time-to-input (the document is open when the editor is usable), with first visible content as the earlier visibility metric and tail-mount completion carrying its own budget; the phases are reported separately and never summed. The acceptance capture template and verify-capture schema gain the same fields; CI suites assert two independent things — the legacy path keeps every existing budget (no gate moves) and the progressive path meets the contract budgets plus the two approved Wave A budgets.
Goals.R-7: Behavioral equivalence under the progressive path: with the toggle enabled, the Stage 0 characterization oracle suites that traverse the open path (canonical Markdown and on-disk bytes, dirty/saved transitions, undo/redo, cursor/selection, word count/TOC, save/Save As/save-and-close/Save All, external change, source round-trip, copy readers) stay green and unchanged — progressive mount must be observationally equivalent to legacy mount for every reader and consumer except timing, and every known-defect family keeps its recorded observedLegacyBehavior (neither repaired nor silently altered).
Goals.R-8: Graph and verification routing: new governed module M-063 (progressive mount subsystem: the Muya mount entry region, the editor open orchestration seam and the Experimental setting surface) is owned by GD-RUNTIME in .grace/graph/runtime.xml, routed through .grace/graph/index.xml, and declares dependencies on M-012 (Muya engine, whose production mount path it extends) and M-060 (harness that proves its budgets); matching verification anchor V-M-063 is owned by VD-PERFORMANCE in .grace/verification/performance.xml with the progressive-path gates, scenarios and content-free markers, routed through .grace/verification/index.xml; M-012 and M-060 narratives record the handoff; V-M-060 is not repurposed and no anchor is duplicated.

Constraints.Item: Default path invariance: with the toggle off (the default, including every fresh session), behavior is exactly today's — the legacy mount serves every open, the existing V-M-025 open-file timing, webkit-perf and webkit-session gates run unchanged and stay green, and no existing budget, marker or suite is weakened, reinterpreted or renamed.

The LargeDocumentContract is normative: its budgets are acceptance gates for the progressive path, never regression excuses for the default path; Chromium/Long-Tasks and WebKit/event-loop-lag-proxy remain separate labelled series and are never merged; no WAL or unsaved-recovery claim appears anywhere (the no-WAL honest contract holds; the atomic old-or-new save stays its own prerequisite change).

Mount-path-only Muya writes: production changes are confined to the mount path (setMarkdown entry, the renderer/mount helpers and the idle-slicing seam) with MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP updated in the same bundle; the parser is not modified (whole-document parse stays); selection, keyboard and event-handler code is touched only where frozen-region interaction strictly requires it, with each such file listed and justified in the plan before execution.

Experimental model binding: local, default-off, session-latched, visible setting; never persists silently; no default flip and no cohort in this change; no release, train admission or publication follows automatically; m048 stays a compile-time capability map and no feature flag is introduced.

Known defects are not repaired: the Stage 0 R-7 families (liveReload overwrite, Move To/rename and metadata false-clean, write ordering, close-by-tab-id, in-place save truncation, Save All transport no-op, string-only external equality, UTF-8 writeback byte loss) keep their dual-recorded behavior under both paths; each repair remains a separate prerequisite change.

Evidence truthfulness: Playwright WebKit results are labelled browser evidence; real WKWebView acceptance records artifact/commit and fixture hashes; the owner-run instrumented capture protocol (bench/acceptance) gains the tail-mount and time-to-input fields; a skipped required phase fails the gate, and an absent owner-side capture is recorded as pending, never as not-run.

Baseline honesty: the numbers this spec cites come from the recorded Stage 0 baseline artifacts under src/renderer/bench/baseline/ and the archived C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 evidence; the plan re-shoots the same-run legacy baseline on then-current main before any progressive-path claim, and the contract's requirement that Wave B starts only after the Wave A baseline is re-shot on the same corpus is honored.

Execution safety (binding on the plan): dedicated isolated worktree (this line's worktree), no destructive reset/checkout in any shared dirty tree, full docs/commit-push-safety.md before any commit/push, hooks intact, protected checks status check honored; English repo artifacts; graph, verification and MODULE_MAP deltas land in the same bundle as the code.

Parallel-session baseline recorded at drafting (2026-10-30, fork/main e7c32b85, worktree branch spec/large-doc-wave-a): active changes C-47, C-50, C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES; grace lint --assertions current = 0 errors; the two-file approved-to-applied status drift in the archived C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 bundle is pre-existing, owned by the archiving session and untouched here; --parallel-preflight is re-run at plan time and every overlap is sequenced, narrowed or completed before approval.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Wave B1 change-source contract, Wave B2 lazy derived-state pipeline (including ensureFreshDocument) and Wave B3 history materialization redesign; Wave B starts only after the Wave A baseline is re-shot on the same corpus.
Wave C large-file warnings and thresholds beyond the mount-path guards, and Wave D virtualization or engine migration.

Any parser change: no fast-path "is this markdown" regex, no token LRU cache, no parser re-architecture (parse is measured-cheap in the recorded baseline — parse_proxy 5–11 ms at the ordinary shape and ~20 ms at the 1 MB shape; those external blueprints are recorded in design context for any future change that needs them, not adopted here).
Chunked or incremental parsing; lazy CodeMirror source mode; virtualized or windowed scrolling.
The default flip of progressive mount, any cohort, release action or train admission.
Repair of the known defect families; WAL/durability work; the atomic old-or-new save (its own prerequisite change).
content-visibility rollout (stays a separate default-off experiment).

The remaining external-blueprint items — GFM table formatter, diff-block highlight colors, link hygiene, daltonism themes, HTML/URL import, file versioning — which are separate future changes outside the large-document line.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Progressive path proven on the corpus: with the toggle enabled, opening every committed fixture (mixed-100k, size-1mb, size-1_7mb-9000sections, giant-list, giant-paragraph, giant-code-block, nested-deep, table-1000rows, semantic-edge, expensive-leaves and the byte-policy materializations where the harness owns decode) emits numeric first-visible-content, time-to-input, tail-mount completion, typing p50/p95 and scroll results in the required Chromium bench-tier and Playwright WebKit runs; the progressive path meets every contract budget at its shape (ordinary: FVC within 400 ms and typing p95 within 50 ms with the +20 percent same-run relative tolerance; 1 MB: open within 1500 ms and typing p95 within 100 ms; stress: open within 4000 ms, typing p95 within 250 ms, longest task within 300 ms, scroll p95 within 50 ms) plus the two owner-approved Wave A budgets once fixed.

Fail-safe and guards proven: an injected chunking failure and an injected mount error each fall back to the legacy mount with the document open and canonical Markdown identical to the legacy path, including the case where edits were accepted after open and before the injected failure (every accepted edit survives the fallback); the depth/traversal guard bounds nested-deep and giant-list mounting (oversize subtrees flatten instead of recursing); no test path yields a blank or partial editor without the fallback marker.

Unmounted-tail interaction proven: navigation into a not-yet-mounted region (scroll jump, search hit, TOC or link jump, restored remembered cursor position, jump-to-end) lands on mounted content via on-demand region mount; continuous scrolling into the tail never overtakes the mount boundary (prefetch keeps mounted content ahead of the viewport, with the scroll frame budget holding); giant-content shapes (giant-paragraph, giant-code-block) show measurable mount progress under the same slicing rather than one monolithic mount; the viewport reading position holds steady while the tail mounts (anchoring asserted by a scripted mid-mount position check); the still-mounting region is visibly marked (reserved layout space or the plan-chosen equivalent), so the document never appears truncated during tail mounting; and model-reading consumers (word count, TOC, search, save) return complete-document results before tail completion.

Default-path invariance: with the toggle off, the full existing suite set is green with no diffs in V-M-025, webkit-perf or webkit-session behavior, and the legacy path's re-shot baseline matches the recorded Stage 0 baseline within the contract's ordinary-document relative tolerance.

Equivalence under the progressive path: the Stage 0 characterization suites pass unchanged with the toggle enabled — same observedLegacyBehavior/desiredInvariant pairs, same canonical bytes, same save/close/external-change outcomes — across the boundary set including save, Save As, save-all, external change, tab switch, source, copy and close.

Experimental surface correct: a visible Experimental section carries the toggle; it is off by default, returns to off after relaunch (no silent persistence), affects only documents opened after the flip, and the UI labels it experimental; the per-session progressive-versus-fallback counter is present and reflects the opens actually served; no other setting, preference key or release surface changes.

Budget decision landed: the owner decision document presents same-run evidence and the two approved budgets, and the approved values are recorded in the LargeDocumentContract in .grace/context/ux-guidelines.xml via the governance step before Wave B begins; the decision document explicitly states that no release or train admission follows.

Routing and contracts: M-063 is routed through .grace/graph/index.xml with its M-012/M-060 dependencies declared and M-012/M-060 narratives updated; V-M-063 is routed through .grace/verification/index.xml with the progressive-path commands, scenarios and content-free markers; MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP updated in every touched production file in the same bundle; no anchor repurposed or duplicated; npm test green; grace lint reports no new errors beyond the recorded drafting baseline.

Evidence honesty: tier labels correct (browser vs native), fixture and artifact hashes recorded in baseline JSON, the acceptance capture schema carries the tail-mount and time-to-input fields, and any pending owner-side WKWebView capture is recorded as pending.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Numeric budget tables for both paths on the committed corpus with fixture hashes; injected-failure fallback proofs; default-path suites green with the legacy baseline re-shot within tolerance; Stage 0 characterization suites green under the progressive path; M-063/V-M-063 routed with content-free markers; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP deltas in the same bundle; the owner decision document with the two approved budgets recorded in ux-guidelines; grace lint clean against the drafting baseline. Assumptions.Assumption: The LargeDocumentContract in .grace/context/ux-guidelines.xml (owner-approved 2026-10-29 from the Stage 0 decision gate) is normative for this change; nothing in this spec modifies it before its own governance step lands the two deferred budgets.

M-063 and V-M-063 are unused across the .grace graph, verification and active-change bundles as of 2026-10-30 on fork/main e7c32b85 — M-060 is taken by Stage 0, M-061/V-M-061 is claimed by the active C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES bundle (hence not available to this change in either landing order), and M-062 is taken elsewhere; the plan re-confirms both ids remain free before claiming them.

The Stage 0 corpus, harness, baseline artifacts and characterization suites are committed and green on main (PR #126 squash 89541d8e, archive PR #127); their behavior is the equivalence oracle for this change.

The Muya mount path can be partitioned at top-level block boundaries without parser changes — the block tree is available before mounting and per-block update machinery already exists for edits; the plan's first task proves this on the real mount path before wide changes, and a disproof escalates back to the owner rather than forcing the design.

The external Claude Code 2.1.312 research digest (2026-10-30, owner-local, outside the repository) is a design reference only: its mechanisms are adapted, none of its code is copied, and none of its numeric thresholds bind this change — every number here is grounded in the Stage 0 baseline or flagged as an owner decision.

Active-change states (C-47, C-50, C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES and any later arrivals), the pre-existing archived-bundle status drift and all parallel-session conditions are re-verified at plan time; this spec's drafting snapshot is not authority.
